title: Friday Truth Brief — Week of November 13, 2026
methodology: Coverage window Mon Nov 9–Sun Nov 15, 2026 (research through Fri Nov 13). Ranked by national salience for an evidence-vs-spin audience. Mix of hard politics AND major culture/news stories twisted by political or culture-war narratives. Known facts cite named sources with URLs/dates. Misrepresentations only when a specific published claim can be checked; otherwise []. Narrative notes describe framing in real coverage. Readers should verify linked sources.

stories.title: Scott Colom unseats Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi; Democrats reach at least 55 Senate seats with only Alaska left
stories.summary: AP called Mississippi’s Senate race for Democrat Scott Colom on Wednesday, Nov. 11, eight days after the election, after counties finished absentee and affidavit (provisional) ballots. Hyde-Smith conceded the same evening. Colom becomes Mississippi’s first Black U.S. senator since Reconstruction and the first Democrat the state has elected to the Senate since 1982. NBC says the win gives Democrats at least 55 seats next year; Alaska is the last uncalled race.
stories.overview: Colom, a north Mississippi district attorney, trailed early and led by just 43 votes after the final election-night update, according to AP; his lead grew as counties finished processing provisional ballots. Mississippi Today reports AP’s call came with 99% of precincts reporting, Colom ahead 49.2% to 48.7% and leading by 4,645 votes Wednesday night, based on uncertified results. Hyde-Smith said in a video, “I respect the decision of Mississippi voters.” The result also fed an intra-Democratic argument over credit: Jon Stewart said Senate leader Chuck Schumer fought ‘half’ of the winners, which PolitiFact rated Mostly False because Schumer recruited the Mississippi and Alaska candidates, among others.

knownFacts.claim: AP called the Mississippi Senate race for Scott Colom on Nov. 11 after counties reported updated results including provisional ballots.
knownFacts.evidence: AP explained its call; NBC projected the same result Nov. 11 at 5:59 p.m. ET.

NBC News — Democrat Scott Colom wins Mississippi Senate race, breaking state’s GOP grip

knownFacts.evidence: Mississippi Today and NBC both report the call and quote her: “While this is not the outcome we worked for or hoped for, I respect the decision of Mississippi voters.”

knownFacts.evidence: Reported by Mississippi Today and NBC News.

misrepresentations.pieceTitle: PolitiFact — Jon Stewart wrong that Chuck Schumer fought half the Democratic Senate winners
misrepresentations.claimMade: Schumer “fought tooth and nail against half of these” Democrats who won Senate races.
misrepresentations.whyInaccurate: PolitiFact found Schumer spearheaded recruitment in North Carolina, Ohio and Iowa plus the Alaska and Mississippi candidates; he initially backed others in Michigan and Maine, and declined to back Flanagan in Minnesota—about three of 12–13 competitive races, not half. Rated Mostly False.

narratives.description: Post-election credit fights inside the winning party.
narratives.example: Claims that party leadership opposed most of the winners.
narratives.howItMisleads: Citing the few primaries leaders lost while ignoring the races they recruited for paints a distorted picture of who built the majority.

stories.title: Trump asks whether the midterms were ‘honest’ days after saying he would accept the results; officials and data push back
stories.summary: On Monday, Nov. 9, Trump wrote on Truth Social, “Does anybody really believe that this ‘Election’ was honest. How could the Polls be so wrong???” and added, “It’s all about the machines.” He offered no evidence. Election-night week he had told The New York Times he was “absolutely willing to accept those results.” In Texas, a viral claim about 2.9 million registrations is being used to question Democratic wins, but the cited federal report doesn’t show fraud.
stories.overview: NBC reports the shift began Saturday, Nov. 7, when Trump reposted an X user questioning uniform vote swings, the same day he replaced chief of staff Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller. A White House official noted Trump had said he would respect results “if they’re honest elections.” Nevada Secretary of State Cisco Aguilar called the claims “completely false.” Pew’s preliminary analysis, cited by NBC, says polls underestimated Democrats’ margin but captured the direction. University of Washington researcher Kate Starbird called the post a “trial balloon.” In Texas, KERA explains the 2.9 million figure is ‘new valid registrations’ from 2022–2024, which includes movers, and was recorded before Trump won Texas in 2024.

knownFacts.claim: Trump questioned the honesty of the midterms on Truth Social on Nov. 9 without offering evidence.
knownFacts.evidence: NBC quotes the post in full and notes election officials nationwide reported largely routine voting.

sources.name: NBC News — Trump casts doubt on election results after saying he was ‘absolutely willing’ to accept them

knownFacts.claim: Trump earlier told The New York Times he was “absolutely willing to accept those results.”
knownFacts.evidence: Quoted by NBC News.

sources.name: NBC News — Trump casts doubt on election results after saying he was ‘absolutely willing’ to accept them

knownFacts.claim: The 2.9 million Texas figure counts ‘new valid registrations’ from 2022 to 2024, not ineligible voters.
knownFacts.evidence: KERA: Texas removed nearly 1.8 million records in the same period; net registration rose about 952,000; an October 2025 SAVE check of 18 million voters led to 117 referrals.

sources.name: KERA / The Texas Newsroom — Why a viral Texas voter registration claim doesn’t prove fraud in the 2026 midterm elections

misrepresentations.outlet: Conservative social media accounts (widely shared posts)
misrepresentations.pieceTitle: KERA / The Texas Newsroom fact check
misrepresentations.claimMade: Texas processed nearly 2.9 million new registrations without proof of citizenship, casting doubt on Democrats’ 2026 wins.
misrepresentations.whyInaccurate: The number is real but comes from 2022–2024 federal survey data that includes people moving into or within Texas. It does not say those registrations were fraudulent and doesn’t examine the 2026 election at all.

narratives.description: Polling misses recast as evidence of rigging.
narratives.example: “How could the Polls be so wrong???”
narratives.howItMisleads: Polls underestimating a winner’s margin is a known polling error, not proof of manipulated ballots. Pew says the polls got the direction right.

stories.title: Trump calls new Iran strikes ‘quite unlikely’ and touts ‘positive momentum’; Tehran denies talks and keeps Hormuz shut
stories.summary: After hosting Qatar’s prime minister Monday, Trump said further strikes on Iran were “quite unlikely” and that the U.S. remains “locked and loaded.” Rubio told G7 ministers the economic campaign is so effective there is “no need for major combat operations.” Iran’s Mohsen Rezaei called reports of ongoing negotiations “a pure lie” and said Hormuz stays closed until the U.S. meets Tehran’s seven conditions.
stories.overview: Al Jazeera reports Trump wrote on Truth Social that Gulf allies prefer the “status quo” of the U.S. blockade of Iranian ports. Rubio called Iran’s demands “totally unrealistic” but said the U.S. is open to diplomacy. NPR says Trump declared the U.S. won the war while keeping the blockade; Iranian officials at COP31 said Iran won. The Guardian reports an adviser to Iran’s chief negotiator claimed the U.S. set a roughly two-week window before a decision on military action—an Iranian claim, not confirmed by Washington. Ship attacks continued; maritime firms counted at least 37 in October. On the U.S. side, Rep. Byron Donalds claimed more oil is moving through Hormuz than before the war; PolitiFact rated that Mostly False.

knownFacts.claim: Trump said further strikes on Iran were “quite unlikely” and cited “positive momentum.”
knownFacts.evidence: Al Jazeera, citing Trump’s Truth Social post and remarks after meeting Qatar’s prime minister.

sources.name: Al Jazeera — Rubio backs blockade, Vance wants deal: Is Trump’s team split on Iran war?
Al Jazeera — Iran denies talks with US, says Hormuz will stay shut until demands are met

knownFacts.claim: Rubio told G7 allies there is “no need for major combat operations” and that economic pressure “is going to get even worse.”
knownFacts.evidence: Reported by Al Jazeera from Rubio’s Paris remarks.

sources.name: Al Jazeera — Rubio backs blockade, Vance wants deal: Is Trump’s team split on Iran war?

knownFacts.claim: Iran denied that talks are underway and said Hormuz will stay closed until its conditions are met.
knownFacts.evidence: Rezaei to Al Mayadeen, reported by Al Jazeera; NPR reports Iranian officials at COP31 insisting on the same conditions.

sources.name: Al Jazeera — Iran denies talks with US, says Hormuz will stay shut until demands are met
NPR — Trump says US won Iran war, Iran responds

knownFacts.claim: An Iranian adviser claims the U.S. proposed about a two-week timeframe before a decision on military action.
knownFacts.evidence: The Guardian reports this as an Iranian assessment; it has not been confirmed by U.S. officials.

misrepresentations.pieceTitle: PolitiFact — Is more oil going through Hormuz than before the Iran war? No.
misrepresentations.claimMade: “There’s more oil going through the Strait (of Hormuz) today than there was pre-war.”
misrepresentations.whyInaccurate: Regional Gulf flows have occasionally matched prewar levels, but average flows through the strait itself remain lower—around 82% of prewar in mid-October per the Wall Street Journal. Rated Mostly False.

narratives.example: Trump says the U.S. won the war; Iran says it won and denies talks.
narratives.howItMisleads: Both sides’ victory claims coexist with a closed strait, an active blockade and continuing ship attacks. The record shows a stalemate, not a settled outcome.

stories.title: House votes 211–204 to send Hegseth impeachment articles to committee, effectively ending Massie’s push this Congress
stories.summary: On Tuesday, Nov. 10, the House referred Rep. Thomas Massie’s articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to committee, short-circuiting a floor vote. The articles cited the Iran war, strikes on alleged drug boats, the capture of Venezuela’s Nicolás Maduro without congressional authorization, and the effort to punish Sen. Mark Kelly. Democrats promise investigations when they take the majority in January.
stories.overview: NPR reports the vote spared Hegseth an up-or-down floor vote that could have come as early as Wednesday. It was Massie’s second try; the first expired when Speaker Mike Johnson called an early recess before the midterms. Hegseth called Massie a “disgruntled and defeated congressman” and said he would execute the operations “again tomorrow.” Trump said, “I’ll stand by him.” ABC reports several Democrats missed the vote, many blaming traffic—relevant because the margin was seven votes. Hakeem Jeffries, expected to be the next speaker, told NPR of Hegseth, “He’s got to go.”

knownFacts.claim: The House voted 211–204 to refer the Hegseth impeachment articles to committee.
knownFacts.evidence: NPR and the House Clerk’s roll call record.

sources.name: NPR — House votes to effectively end the impeachment effort against Pete Hegseth
Office of the Clerk, U.S. House — Roll call vote 317

knownFacts.claim: Massie’s articles cited the Iran war, boat strikes, the Maduro capture without authorization, and the effort to punish Sen. Mark Kelly.
knownFacts.evidence: Summarized by NPR.

sources.name: NPR — House votes to effectively end the impeachment effort against Pete Hegseth

knownFacts.claim: Several Democrats missed the vote.
knownFacts.evidence: ABC News reports many cited traffic.

sources.name: ABC News — Several Democrats missed the crucial Hegseth impeachment vote. Many blamed traffic

narratives.example: Supporters cast the referral as Hegseth surviving impeachment.
narratives.howItMisleads: A referral is a procedural move that avoided a vote on the merits; it neither clears nor convicts him, and new House majorities can revisit oversight in January.

stories.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO after affair reports; DOJ says it hasn’t determined whether Alice Huang was a Chinese spy
stories.summary: Nvidia announced Nov. 12 that co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO, president and board member, effective immediately; CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO. The exit followed reports of an affair with Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive U.S. officials reportedly suspect of working for Chinese intelligence, and a second reported affair with an Nvidia executive. Attorney General Todd Blanche said the FBI is investigating but no conclusion has been reached.
stories.overview: The Verge reports the board accepted Huang’s resignation after a late Wednesday meeting and named former Synopsys CEO Harvey C. Jones Nvidia’s first board chair. Huang admitted Nov. 8 that he had been “unfaithful.” The story turned political fast because of Huang’s close relationship with Trump and questions about chip exports to China. On the record: Blanche said the DOJ has not determined whether Alice Huang was a spy; Trump said “I don’t know if that’s been determined yet”; Beijing denies it; and Singapore said its separate investigation of her did not concern espionage (Reuters). Much online commentary is treating the spy allegation as proven.

knownFacts.claim: Huang resigned as CEO, president and director; Colette Kress is interim CEO and the board is searching for a permanent chief.
knownFacts.evidence: Nvidia’s announcement and The Verge.

sources.name: NVIDIA Investor Relations — NVIDIA Announces CEO Transition
The Verge — Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns amid spy, affair scandals

knownFacts.claim: The Justice Department has not determined whether Alice Huang was a Chinese spy; the FBI is investigating.
knownFacts.evidence: Blanche at a Nov. 12 press conference and Trump in an interview, per Reuters.

sources.name: Reuters via The Economic Times — US yet to determine if Alice Huang was Chinese spy, Trump, Blanche say

knownFacts.claim: Singapore said its investigation of Alice Huang did not concern espionage; Beijing denies she is a spy.
knownFacts.evidence: Reuters.

sources.name: Reuters via The Economic Times — US yet to determine if Alice Huang was Chinese spy, Trump, Blanche say

narratives.description: An unproven spy allegation treated as settled.
narratives.example: Posts calling Alice Huang a confirmed Chinese agent and using that to argue chip-export policy was compromised.
narratives.howItMisleads: The allegation rests on reporting citing U.S. intelligence officials. The attorney general says it hasn’t been determined. Treat it as an open investigation until officials say otherwise.

stories.title: Alaska, the last uncalled Senate race: Peltola’s lead grows to about 5,800 votes ahead of Nov. 18 final count
stories.summary: Democrat Mary Peltola led Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan 49.1% to 46.8% in first-choice votes after a Nov. 12 count, a margin of about 5,800 with more than 256,000 ballots counted. Final counting and any ranked-choice tabulation are set for Nov. 18; certification is due Nov. 25. Preliminary ballot-level data suggest Peltola stays ahead even after ranked-choice transfers.
stories.overview: The Anchorage Daily News reports Peltola’s lead grew by about 1,825 votes from Wednesday to Thursday. If no one tops 50%, the lowest finishers are eliminated: Republican Gerald Heikes (about 2.1%) and Dan J. Sullivan (about 1.6%), the similarly named candidate at the center of the ‘decoy’ controversy. Courts are busy too. A federal judge dismissed the Justice Department’s pre-election suit to delay certification, and DOJ appealed to the Ninth Circuit. On Nov. 11 a state judge denied Peltola’s campaign’s request for names of voters whose absentee ballots were rejected, saying the records are preliminary and not public during counting.

stories.title: Trump threatens to double tariffs on Mexico unless it stops a migrant caravan of about 1,500 people
stories.summary: On Nov. 12, Trump posted that Mexico must stop migrants walking north “NOW” or tariffs would be “IMMEDIATELY DOUBLED,” naming Texas’ incoming Democratic governor, Gina Hinojosa. Reuters says about 1,500 people, mostly Central Americans, left Tapachula on Tuesday, hoping the Democratic Congress opens new paths. Mexico’s President Claudia Sheinbaum says no caravans have reached the U.S. border since Trump returned and Mexico is working to return the migrants home.
stories.overview: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said the caravan “will NOT be allowed to enter.” Sheinbaum promised “no acts of repression.” Reuters notes the administration’s policies have mostly stopped the flow of migrants to the southern border, and that Trump told 60 Minutes that the deportation force had been “too tough” and he was open to an immigration deal with Democrats. The U.S. and Mexico are negotiating a trade deal after Trump declined in July to extend USMCA.

knownFacts.claim: Trump threatened to double tariffs on Mexico if it does not stop the caravan.
knownFacts.evidence: Reuters quotes the post.

knownFacts.claim: An estimated 1,500 people left Tapachula on Nov. 10.
knownFacts.evidence: Reuters.

sources.name: Reuters via Investing.com — Trump threatens to double tariffs on Mexico if it does not halt migrants

knownFacts.claim: Sheinbaum said no migrant caravans have reached the U.S. border since Trump returned to office.
knownFacts.evidence: Reuters.

sources.name: Reuters via Investing.com — Trump threatens to double tariffs on Mexico if it does not halt migrants

narratives.description: A walking group that just left southern Mexico framed as an imminent invasion tied to Democrats’ win.
narratives.example: “Here we go again!” and naming Texas’ “VERY LIBERAL NEW GOVERNOR.”
narratives.howItMisleads: The incoming governor doesn’t take office until January, and Mexico says caravans haven’t reached the border in this term. The real policy fight is over tariffs and a pending trade deal.

stories.title: Dave Chappelle and a liberal podcast face backlash over Charlie Kirk assassination jokes; Erika Kirk calls it ‘moral decay’
stories.summary: At a Nov. 7 Madison Square Garden show, Dave Chappelle said that since Charlie Kirk was murdered, “I feel better,” according to leaked fan videos. Days earlier, “I’ve Had It” hosts Jennifer Welch and Angie Sullivan laughed at a joke about Kirk, then apologized after sponsors including Cash App left. Erika Kirk condemned “leftist podcasters, comedians, and commentators” laughing about political assassination.
stories.overview: The LA Times notes the show was supposed to be phone-free. Piers Morgan called the remark “disgusting,” and Elon Musk wrote “Dave Chappelle is cruel.” NBC notes some conservatives had embraced Chappelle for his jokes about transgender people. Michael Che also joked about Kirk’s murder in his October Netflix special. Charlie Kirk was shot and killed in September 2025 at Utah Valley University; Tyler Robinson has been charged. Chappelle’s representatives didn’t respond to requests for comment.

knownFacts.claim: Chappelle said “I feel better” since Kirk’s murder at a Nov. 7 Madison Square Garden show.
knownFacts.evidence: Fan videos quoted by the LA Times and NBC News.

knownFacts.evidence: LA Times and NBC News.

narratives.howItMisleads: The documented cases are specific people, and some drew criticism and sponsor exits from across the spectrum. Chappelle was recently praised by conservatives. Judge the speakers, not a whole political camp.

stories.title: Viral claim says gas companies inflated prices to make voters blame Trump; prices have been falling since September
stories.summary: Posts circulating after the election said falling gas prices prove “the gas companies purposely increased the prices so you would blame Trump and vote blue.” PolitiFact rated it False. The U.S. average peaked at $4.48 on Sept. 21 and fell every week before the Nov. 3 election, dropping below $4 the week of Nov. 9.
stories.overview: PolitiFact says the posts came from accounts including one named “Republican Party” that isn’t official, and conservative influencer David J. Harris Jr., who said the prices “had nothing to do with the Iran war.” Analysts including GasBuddy’s Patrick De Haan point to normal fall declines (less driving, cheaper winter blend) and higher Middle East oil exports. The national average was about $3.94 on Nov. 11.

knownFacts.claim: U.S. gas prices peaked Sept. 21 at $4.48 and fell weekly before the election.
knownFacts.evidence: PolitiFact, citing price data.

sources.name: PolitiFact — Falling gas prices aren’t proof gas companies inflated prices to hurt Trump

knownFacts.claim: The national average fell below $4 the week of Nov. 9, about $3.94 on Nov. 11.
knownFacts.evidence: PolitiFact.

sources.name: PolitiFact — Falling gas prices aren’t proof gas companies inflated prices to hurt Trump

misrepresentations.outlet: Social media posts (incl. an unofficial “Republican Party” Instagram account and David J. Harris Jr.)
misrepresentations.pieceTitle: PolitiFact — Falling gas prices aren’t proof gas companies inflated prices to hurt Trump
misrepresentations.claimMade: Gas companies purposely raised prices so voters would blame Trump and vote Democratic.
misrepresentations.whyInaccurate: Prices began falling in late September, well before the election, following seasonal patterns and Gulf export increases. U.S. gas companies have little power over globally set oil prices. Rated False.

narratives.example: Prices dropped after the election, so they must have been rigged before it.
narratives.howItMisleads: The decline started six weeks earlier. Picking a post-election starting point hides the trend.

stories.title: Judge rules Lindsay Clancy can be retried for murder, rejecting her double-jeopardy bid
stories.summary: On Nov. 9, Massachusetts Superior Court Judge William F. Sullivan denied Lindsay Clancy’s motion to dismiss, ruling that the September jury deadlock created a “manifest need” for a mistrial, so a retrial does not violate double jeopardy. No retrial date has been set.
stories.overview: Clancy’s defense never disputed that she killed her three children in January 2023; it argued she was not criminally responsible because of postpartum psychosis. The first trial ended with one holdout juror, whom other jurors accused of ignoring evidence; he later said through his attorney he “didn’t have any doubts” about her guilt. The judge said removing a juror “for their thought process” would have been beyond his authority. The case remains a flashpoint in online fights over maternal mental health and women’s accountability.

knownFacts.claim: Judge Sullivan ruled Nov. 9 that a retrial does not violate double jeopardy.
knownFacts.evidence: 16-page ruling quoted by USA TODAY; also reported by AP.

sources.name: USA TODAY — Lindsay Clancy can be retried for murder, judge rules
AP News — Judge’s ruling could clear the way for Lindsay Clancy to be tried again in the deaths of her 3 kids

knownFacts.claim: The defense argued Clancy wasn’t criminally responsible because of postpartum psychosis, and didn’t dispute the killings.
knownFacts.evidence: USA TODAY.

sources.name: USA TODAY — Lindsay Clancy can be retried for murder, judge rules

narratives.description: A legal question pulled into the gender and mental-health war.
narratives.example: Online camps calling the ruling either justice for the children or punishment of postpartum illness.
narratives.howItMisleads: The ruling decided only whether a hung jury allows a new trial. It said nothing about whether Clancy was legally insane. That question goes back to a jury.
